chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, and Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Zurara, from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon them).

Regarding a man who married a virgin woman, then divorced her before consummating the marriage with three divorces, one per month. He (peace be upon him) said: 'She becomes irrevocably divorced from him at the first divorce, and the other two are superfluous, and he is a suitor who may marry her whenever she wishes and he wishes, with a new dower.' It was said to him (peace be upon him): 'Does he have the right to revert to her if he divorces her with one divorce before three months pass?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No. Rather, he would have the right to revert to her if he had first consummated the marriage. As for before he consummates it, there is no reversion for him to her. She has become irrevocably divorced from him from the moment he divorces her.'

key_terms.بَانَتْ مِنْهُ: she became irrevocably divorced from him
key_terms.رَجْعَةَ: right of reversion (to take back wife without new contract)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on triple divorce before consummation in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the jurisprudential nuance that in the case of a virgin wife, the first divorce before consummation effects an immediate and irrevocable separation (bayn al-zawjayn), rendering the subsequent two divorces merely superfluous rather than cumulative. Consequently, the husband loses the right of simple reversion (raj'a) entirely, as this right is contingent upon consummation, requiring a new marriage contract (aqd jadid) and dower (mahr jadid) for remarriage. This ruling highlights the distinct legal status of pre-consummation divorce in Shia fiqh, distinguishing it from the three-stage process applicable after consummation.
